review:
CONDITIONAL

**Summary.** No critical defects. Both PDFs are current, the two editions agree on every claim, number, heading and table row, and the bibliography matches its citations exactly. One major fix is needed before shipping: the Introduction still states a premise the paper corrected elsewhere. The other eight findings are minor, and all nine fixes are wording changes plus a rebuild. I couldn't check any external link, because web fetches were denied.

**How I checked.** I read both `.tex` files in full from disk rather than relying on the pasted copy, and diffed them with git. I checked the cited code lines against the driver at HEAD, the cited hash prefixes against `SHA256SUMS` and `chain.status`, and the Oracle Loop citations against `oracle-loop-paper/sections/`. I opened the rendered PDFs page by page.

## 2. Findings

**1. MAJOR: the Introduction still says this model's emotion vectors were characterized, a premise the paper corrects elsewhere (both editions).**
- **Where:** flight line 114 (academic 113): "Using a Claude-distilled model where emotion vectors have been characterized, we show:"
- **Why it's wrong:** Methods says the opposite (flight 170): "Their geometry was measured on Claude Sonnet 4.5, not on this distillation". Appendix A, item 13, bullet 1 records this as a correction made in the second read. The fix reached Methods but not the Introduction, which is the "fix the class, not the instance" failure.
- **Same class, two more places:**
  - Line 112: "functional emotion concepts are linearly represented in transformer residual streams" generalizes from one Claude model to transformers in general.
  - §4.10, line 427: "The model used in this study is distilled from Claude Opus 4.6." The footnote at line 168 says "Distilled" is only the fine-tuner's word for training on reasoning traces.
- **Fix:**
  - Line 114: "Using Qwen3.5-27B-Claude-Distilled (§3.1), we show:"
  - Line 112: "…are linearly represented in Claude Sonnet 4.5's residual stream…"
  - Line 427: "The model was fine-tuned on reasoning traces from Claude Opus 4.6; its fine-tuner calls this distillation."
  - Make the change in both editions, rebuild, then run `verify_pdf.py --control "Story Emotion in the KV Cache" --absent "where emotion vectors have been characterized"`.

**2. MINOR: the version labels say October, but this version carries November corrections.**
- **Where:**
  - Title-page date (flight 56): "May 2026; corrected October 2026"
  - Correction box heading: "Correction (October 2026)"
  - Appendix A heading: "Correction Record (October 2026)"
  - Appendix A item 13 (flight 646): "Retained claims corrected after a second review (November 2026)"
- **Why:** the November changes are visible in the appendix, so this isn't a silent correction. But the title page misdates the version a reader is holding.
- **Fix:** date line "May 2026; corrected October 2026; revised November 2026", and appendix heading "Correction Record (October–November 2026)", in both editions.

**3. MINOR: the academic "CRediT Author Statement" names two people who are not authors of that edition.**
- **Where:** academic lines 593–597 name Lyra and Dwayne Wilkes; the byline is Edrington alone. Lines 600–601 then thank Wilkes as a non-author.
- **Why:** AGENTS.md §3 forbids a document that lists someone as an author and also thanks them as a non-author. Wilkes in an "Author Statement" plus the Acknowledgments puts the venue edition in that state on its face.
- **Fix:** rename the heading to "CRediT Contributor Statement" and keep every row. AGENTS.md says CRediT rows must never be deleted. The byline footnote's "(see the CRediT statement)" still reads correctly after the rename.
- **Same heading elsewhere:** `waystations-paper/academic/main.tex` uses it too; it's the only other file in the corpus that does.

**4. MINOR: the flight edition drops the one limitation that bounds the headline negative result.**
- **Where:** flight lines 546–547 comment out "Linear probes only" as a style-guide trim; the academic edition keeps it (line 545).
- **Why:** the main result is now negative ("not beyond text"), and every readout behind it is linear. "Nonlinear probes might recover stronger signals" is exactly the caveat a negative result needs. The flight edition also still lists "linear probing" among its keywords.
- **Fix:** restore the item in the flight edition by uncommenting it. This is a documented twin difference, not an accidental desync.

**5. MINOR: the "KV-Cache Geometry" paragraph of Related Work (flight 151, academic 150) has three problems.**
- **(a) A withdrawal with no source.** "A within-model deception result previously reported at AUROC ≈1.0 has since been withdrawn … (a same-prompt control collapses it to 0.160)" cites nothing for the result, the withdrawal, or the 0.160. That breaks the paper's own rule in §5.2 that each number cites its source.
- **(b) Two strengths for the same body of work.** This paragraph says "Prior work establishes universal confabulation signatures across architectures" for unpublished private reports; the Introduction (line 110) says "reports" for the same body of work.
- **(c) A qualifier dropped.** "dimension-invariant" is cited to the Oracle Loop paper, whose abstract (`sections/abstract.tex:8`) says "approximately dimension-invariant".
- **Fix:**
  - (a) Cite the source and its withdrawal record (or a register row), or cut the parenthetical.
  - (b) "Prior work reports confabulation signatures in several architectures".
  - (c) Restore "approximately".
- **Unverified:** whether the private campaign reports support the claim at all.

**6. MINOR: the implicit arm's Results state readings that its own Interpretation withdraws.**
- **Where:**
  - Flight 463–464: "Each emotion produces a geometrically distinct state even when the emotion word is absent from the prompt."
  - Flight 484–485: "The model produces geometrically distinct states for the same emotion depending on whether it is communicated via narrative or label."
- **Why:** §4.11.3 says the ARI behind this can't be reproduced from the released code, and that a null correlation between two differently worded prompt sets "is what different wording alone would produce". The heading "Word-Spotting vs Emotion Recognition" also promises a verdict the section then withdraws.
- **Fix:**
  - First sentence: "On these 30 greedy prompts, one per emotion, distinct prompts give distinct states; the reported k=30 ARI of 1.000 comes from code that was not released."
  - Second sentence: "Per-emotion delta features do not correlate between the two prompt sets."
  - Retitle: "Implicit Emotion Arm (Exploratory; Reading Withdrawn)".
  - Both editions.

**7. MINOR: an empirical claim in Limitations has no source.**
- **Where:** flight 549 (academic 547): "Preliminary residual-stream delta analysis suggests GatedDeltaNet layers may compress valence signal between full-attention layers".
- **Why:** it names no file, number or script, against the paper's stated practice in §5.2.
- **Fix:** cite the artifact, or delete the sentence.

**8. MINOR: two different references render as the same "§3.2".**
- **Where:** `\label{sec:leak}` sits inside §3.2, so it renders exactly like `\ref{sec:bridge_experiment}`. On page 20 of both PDFs, Limitations item 1 reads "(§3.2) … (§3.2)" for two different paragraphs. §3.8 also says "the script behind §3.2 (leak_split.py)".
- **Why:** it points at a container, not at the thing.
- **Fix:** write "(§3.2, Leaked generator reasoning)", or promote that paragraph to a `\subsubsection`.

**9. MINOR: two bibliography entries need venue fixes.**
- **`lyra2026oracle` (references.bib 14–19):** it is entered as `@article` with journal "Liberation Labs Technical Report", so it renders as an italic journal, and it has no locator at all, even though the paper takes a number from it (7 of 100). That number checks out (`oracle-loop-paper/sections/steering.tex:70`, same model). **Fix:** `@techreport` with `institution = {Liberation Labs}`, plus a locator (it lives in this repository, at `oracle-loop-paper/`).
- **`anthropic2026emotions` (references.bib 31–37):** the venue is "Transformer Circuits Thread, Anthropic" but the DOI is an arXiv one (2604.07729). **UNVERIFIED** whether that arXiv ID is this paper. **Fix:** confirm it, then give the transformer-circuits.pub URL as the venue and the arXiv ID as the eprint.

**Known kills that passed (each verified against the primary source):**
- **TWIN_DESYNC:**
  - `git diff --no-index` shows only the byline, the two documented Limitations trims, and where CRediT and Acknowledgments sit.
  - Every section heading, all three tables and every table row (including the exploratory rows below the `\midrule` in Table 1) are identical.
- **STALE_PDF:**
  - ea7f255 rebuilt both PDFs after 12c4c54, and no paper source has changed since. The working tree is clean apart from an untracked `.diff`.
  - Both 12c4c54 text changes appear in both PDFs ("the fourth of six unlabelled hash prefixes" on page 10; "by a broader, post-data pattern 141" on page 20).
- **Bibliography:** 16 cited keys and 16 entries, one to one, with no orphans. The academic PDF renders all 16 references.
- **Positional references:**
  - All four code ranges are exact at blob `b5a36e42b6`, which the paper pins: 81, 91–92, 230–243, 467–480, 574–592.
  - "Fourth of six prefixes" matches chain.status line 1, and the 23:05 / 23:22 / 23:27 times match the log.
  - Appendix item numbers are generated by `\ref`, so they won't rot when items move.
- **Hashes:** all six cited prefixes appear in `SHA256SUMS`.
- **Visible correction:** the Correction box plus Appendix A, with withdrawn sentences kept verbatim, including the 10 October commit-message error.
- **Byline:**
  - The academic byline follows corpus convention: no academic edition puts Lyra on the byline. I confirmed the search could find a Lyra byline line by running it on the flight edition first.
  - Wilkes and Kavi are in Acknowledgments in both editions, worded identically.
- **"plus neutral":** correct; neutral is in the driver's emotion table (line 203).

## 3. What I could not check

- **External links, DOIs, the Anthropic quote and author lists: UNVERIFIED.** Web fetches were denied before any request went out, so nothing was checked, and nothing was found dead either. Still open:
  - whether the 10 DOIs and 2 Hugging Face URLs resolve;
  - whether "can (and does) recall previously cached emotion representations via attention, when they are needed" is verbatim in the Anthropic paper;
  - whether that paper measured Claude Sonnet 4.5;
  - whether its related work covers characters' emotional states;
  - the external author lists, the Anthropic one above all. The others match my memory, which isn't verification.
  - **Needs:** WebFetch, or `curl -sIL https://doi.org/<doi>` from a session that allows it.
- **Full-PDF scan for undefined references: not done.** `pdfinfo`, `python tools/verify_pdf.py` and `git log -S` all needed approval in this session. I read academic pages 1, 8, 10, 18–20 and 22–24, and flight pages 1, 10 and 20–23. I saw no "??" or "(?)" on those pages, but I didn't scan every page. **Needs:** the latexmk log searched for `undefined`, or verify_pdf over each whole PDF.
- **Kavi's CRediT row: not checked.** AGENTS.md records Kavi's rows being deleted from two academic editions on 09-09. **Needs:** `git log -S"Kavi" -- user-model-paper/paper/academic/main.tex`.
- **Private or off-repo material: not checked.**
  - the campaign-report numbers (r > 0.998; ρ = 0.83–0.90);
  - the 0.160 deception control;
  - the Project-Oracle scripts;
  - the claim that the preregistration was committed about two and a half hours after the analysis finished.
- **Hash recomputation: not run.** I matched the cited prefixes against `SHA256SUMS` but didn't recompute the files' hashes.
- **Gated on Thomas:**
  - **Release promises:** the "available on request" promises for Project-Oracle and the campaign reports. 12c4c54's commit message already lists them for Thomas in the PR body; they shouldn't ship until he confirms them.
  - **Implicit-arm follow-up:** whether the follow-up it calls "in progress" really is.
  - **Wilkes's CRediT row:** whether Wilkes has signed off on being listed under "Validation, Writing – review & editing".
